outcome: Maternal morbidity (PPH, DIC, HELLP, pulmonary edema, PRES, ARF, gluteal abscess)
Fetal outcomes (live birth rate, birth weight, APGAR score, NICU admission, neonatal death, RDS, LBW)
cohort: The study included 50 pregnant women diagnosed with eclampsia with more than 20 weeks of gestation and up to 42 days postpartum who presented to the hospital.
finding: The study found a 0.9% prevalence of eclampsia, with a 4% maternal mortality rate and an 11% neonatal mortality rate, primarily due to RDS in low birth weight babies, emphasizing the importance of early and intensive management.
birth_weight: Majority of live births weighed between 2.1-2.5 kg; most neonatal mortality occurred in babies weighing less than 1 kg.
gest_age: Inclusion criteria specified more than 20 weeks of gestation; majority of eclampsia cases (48%) were between 33-36 weeks of gestation.
